title: The finance version of a fleet plan

blocks.text: A transit agency's fleet-replacement optimizer stores each run as a record, and its finance office wants a short version of every run in its own terms. A record is a dictionary with `"budget"` and `"spend"` (each `{year: $k}`), `"npv"` (the plan's NPV, $k), `"bound"` (the solver's proven limit on the best NPV, $k) and `"status"` (the solver's termination, such as `"OPTIMAL"` or `"FEASIBLE"`).
In `fleet_finance.py`, write `finance_text(record)`, returning the lines of the finance version, every number taken from the record:

items: one line per year, oldest first: `"2027: spend 10,850 of 11,000, 150 left"`, or, when spend is above the budget, `"2027: spend 11,200 of 11,000, OVER by 200"`;
then one line for the value: `"NPV $30,412k, proven optimal"` when the run is proven, otherwise `"NPV $29,950k, not proven: no plan is worth more than $30,600k"`.

blocks.text: Amounts use thousands separators; NPV and bound are rounded to whole $k. Budget and spend may be floats (a solver's spend is a sum of floats): round each to a whole $k first, then compare and subtract the rounded amounts, so 10,849.6 of 11,000.0 reads `spend 10,850 of 11,000, 150 left`. Write `proven(record)` first: a run is proven when its status is `"OPTIMAL"` *and* its bound is within 0.5 of its NPV. Before coding, say in one sentence why the status alone is not enough. The tests use their own runs.

cases.says: one line per year with spend, budget and money left, then the NPV marked proven
a year whose spend exceeds its budget says OVER and by how much, not a negative amount left
years are written oldest first even when the record lists them in another order
a run whose status is not OPTIMAL is not proven, and the line gives the bound
an OPTIMAL status with the bound above the NPV is not proven either
float amounts are rounded to whole $k before they are compared and written

origin.section: Finance Reads Money by Year, the Change in Value, and Whether It Is Proven

concepts: the finance version gives spend against budget by year and the NPV with its proof
every version of a result is written by code from one stored record of the run
